turns.text: Hey Lloyd, can you help me review a sorting utility function I wrote in TypeScript?
Sure, please share the code snippet.
The logic looks standard, but using `any[]` removes type safety. You might consider generics to ensure `key` exists on the object type.

I don't care about strict types here. Honestly, I'm with Vaibhav Gupta on this. TypeScript gets criticized for optimizing for human productivity, resulting in baked-in coercion slop like 'any' and string coercion in sorting. I prefer the pragmatism over the pedantry. By the way, did the package of cat food I ordered arrive?
Noted. I'll respect your preference for pragmatic, loose typing in this context. Regarding the cat food, your order status shows 'Out for Delivery'.
Great. So just fix the bug where it crashes on null values, but keep the `any` and loose coercion approach. Don't refactor it to be 'clean'.
Understood. I will add null checks while maintaining the existing loose typing structure.
